extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and recordkeeping standards for maintaining the patent application file wrapper, documenting searches (classification, limited, text, database), and rules for public use proceedings and related filings under MPEP guidance. Focused on examiner and applicant/petitioner obligations during prosecution and reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antedating when reference is commonly owned (37 CFR 1.130 requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the rejection to be overcome is under 35 U.S.C. 103 in view of a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that is commonly owned, 37 CFR 1.130(a) requires: (1) a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321(c); and (2) an oath or declaration stating inter alia that the inventor named in the application or patent under reexamination is the prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inventor in the application/patent under reexamination must have invented the claimed subject matter before the actual date of invention of the reference claims. The affidavit/declaration may be signed by inventor(s), attorney/agent of record, or assignee(s) of the entire interest. 37 CFR 1.130 also interacts with interference rules (37 CFR 41.206) and antedating restrictions in 37 CFR 1.131 (anticommon-claiming requirements). See MPEP § 804.03 and § 706.02(l)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on establishing prior inventor dates (35 U.S.C. 104 geographic/date restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant/patent owner may not establish a date of invention in certain foreign countries for the purpose of being a 'prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104' except as limited by NAFTA/WTO date rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (A) cannot establish a date of invention in a foreign country other than a NAFTA or WTO member country; (B) cannot establish a date of invention in a WTO member country (other than a NAFTA country) earlier than January 1, 1996; (C) cannot establish a date of invention in a NAFTA country (other than the U.S.) earlier than December 8, 1993. These limitations apply when determining whether a reference is disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) or 37 CFR 1.130.

rubrics_metrics.name: File wrapper contents — entry, numbering, and expungement
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers legally entered on the 'Contents' of the file wrapper are given a paper number and should not be withdrawn or expunged except with special authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter transient papers that should not become permanent on the Contents. Expungement is only allowed under limited authority (see 37 CFR 1.59 for unintentional submissions or proprietary information not important to patentability decisions). Certain oaths executed abroad may be returned with a copy retained. See MPEP § 724 for petitions to expunge. For IFW processing, see IFW Manual sections referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and handling of papers and duplicates in the file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and applicant communications are fastened to the left (center) fold in inverse chronological order; Office communications are fastened to the right in inverse chronological order; duplicates are normally destroyed except in specified late-reply/duplicate scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When amendments are submitted in duplicate, the copy is destroyed except when the duplicate is received within the time period for reply and the original is late — then both are placed in the file with the original entered and reference to the copy. At allowance, only papers required by the printer are placed in the left side (center section). Drawings are kept on top of the right side papers for examiner convenience. See IFW Manual sections for image processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings/prints handling and endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prints of drawings are fastened inside the file wrapper; white paper prints are kept on top of the right-side papers; all prints and inked sketches filed to be part of the record should be endorsed with the application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of Initial Patent Examination fastens drawing prints. See MPEP § 608.02(m) for endorsement specifics and IFW Manual for image processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers not returned and notification (Form paragraph 7.214)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers in an application that has received a filing date ordinarily will not be returned; Form paragraph 7.214 may notify applicant of this, and copies will be furnished at applicant's expense if applicant has not preserved copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 37 CFR 1.19 for fees and MPEP § 724.05 for petitions to expunge information. Use form 7.214 (Pro Se) as appropriate to notify applicants that papers are not returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for correcting data on the file wrapper or PALM bib-data sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: If an error is noticed in data on the file wrapper or PALM bib-data sheet, the examiner should correct it in red ink and forward the application to the TC technical support staff for database correction and printing of a new bib-data sheet or adhesive label, following series-specific procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction methods vary by application series: for 08/ or earlier series, make correction in red ink on file wrapper and forward for PALM correction; for 09/series correct on PALM bib-data sheet and forward; for 10/ and above series correct on file wrapper and forward for printing an adhesive label. Examples of instances requiring correction include changes in inventorship (37 CFR 1.48), filing date corrections, prior U.S. application number errors, and corrections to benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c). See MPEP §§ 605.04(g), 202.02, 201.11, and 1302.09.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index of Claims maintenance and marking rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Index of Claims inside the file wrapper must be kept up to date as a reliable index of all claims and amendments; preprinted original claim numbers and adjacent final numbering columns should be used; independent claims should be encircled in red ink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claims are rewritten under 37 CFR 1.121(c), do not strike original claim number but note 'Amend. 1' etc. For cancellations, strike-through the original number in red. Place final patent claim numbers in the 'Final' column at allowance. Mark the highest numbered claim added by each amendment with a red line and mark amendment letter opposite the first claim of each amendment. See MPEP § 719.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording field of search (OACS Search Notes) and search updates
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits, the examiner must record the areas searched in the OACS 'Search Notes' page, indicate dates of search and examiner initials; in subsequent actions indicate updates and additional fields searched with dates and initials, including databases and search queries/classifications used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record searches clearly to provide a complete, accurate, and uniform record of what has been searched and considered for each application. Care must be taken to indicate where and when searches were conducted/updated. See MPEP § 904 and IFW Manual section references for image processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing 'SEARCHED' box vs 'SEARCH NOTES' box entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches are categorized into those recorded in the 'SEARCHED' box and those in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box, with each category having specific documentation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I. 'SEARCHED' BOX: record classification searches (complete search of all documents in a subclass) with class/subclass, date, and initials. Also record updated searches from parent applications using '(updated from parent S.N. ...)' or patent number if parent patented. II. 'SEARCH NOTES' BOX: record limited classification searches (class/subclass plus annotation), text-only database searches (enter 'See search history printout(s)' plus date/initials and include printout in file), consultations with other examiners (record class/subclass and '(consulted)' and optionally the examiner and art unit), manual literature searches with sufficient bibliographic detail, and reviews of art cited in parent applications (record parent application number and 'refs. checked' or exceptions). Include examples and formatting conventions as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search history printout minimum content and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Any time an electronic search was performed (limited classification or text search), a complete search history printout must be included in the application file (scanned into IFW) containing specified minimum information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum required information: (1) all search logic or chemical structure or sequence(s) used as the database query; (2) all names of the file(s) searched and the database service; (3) the date the search was made or updated; and (4) the examiner's initials (unless automatically provided by the search engine). Do not merely list the tool/database name without the query. Search history printouts should be devoid of result printouts to limit bulk. If several search statements exist, circle in black ink those statements whose results were reviewed. For nucleotide/peptide searches stored in SCORE, record 'See sequence search results in SCORE' with date and initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database-specific documentation and filling missing history elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Because different database services display different elements in history commands, examiners must ensure missing elements (database name, date, file names, etc.) are added to the printout or supplied via additional transcript/logoff commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 in the MPEP lists history commands and which elements are missing per service (e.g., Dialog/Questel-Orbit may not display file names or dates in history; WEST displays the date the history was printed rather than the date of search). Missing elements can be written on the printout in black ink or supplied by including parts of the search transcript (e.g., logoff). Ensure the name of the file is provided (file number alone is insufficient) and the date of search is documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet search engine documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For Internet search engines (e.g., Google), print the first page and any pages that include names of webpages reviewed, and ensure the printout contains the search engine name, search logic, and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the browser print icon or file-print command. If the engine name, search logic, or date are missing, write the missing information on the printout. Circle with black ink all webpages reviewed. Include these printouts in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of non-patent literature and other databases (CD-ROMs, specialized resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: For other publicly accessible or specialized databases (CD-ROMs, STIC-provided NPL searches, etc.), record sufficient identification of material searched and the search query/request so the search can be updated, including location and form of the database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: cite CD-ROM title/version, type, date searched, and search terms; for abstracting publications list title and index terms used; for books/periodicals list title/author/volume/pages/date. For STIC searches, include complete search history printouts provided by EIC/STIC staff and note where full text of citations can be obtained. Browsing/cursory searches can be noted collectively (e.g., 'Browsed STIC shelves under QA 76.5') but detailed searches must be recorded specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is not recorded in the application file (IDS consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application file does not record certain information, such as indications of consideration or nonconsideration of prior art citations submitted in Information Disclosure Statements (37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For where such considerations are documented, see MPEP § 609 et seq. Do not expect IDS handling/consideration status to be present in the search notes/field-of-search entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use proceedings — petition requirements and filing conditions (37 CFR 1.292)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to institute public use proceedings (ex parte or inter partes) under 37 CFR 1.292 must make a prima facie showing (supported by affidavits/declarations) that the claimed invention was in public use or on sale more than one year before filing, and must meet filing, service, fee, and timing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements to have the petition entered in the application file: (1) accompanied by fee per 37 CFR 1.17(j); (2) served on the applicant per 37 CFR 1.248 or filed in duplicate if service not possible; (3) submitted prior to publication of the application or mailing of notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311, whichever occurs first. Duplicate copies should only be submitted after diligent effort to serve applicant. Notice of petition may be entered in lieu of bulky papers; any public use papers not physically entered will be publicly available when the file wrapper is available. The Director has discretion to institute proceedings and may designate officials, set hearing times, and use part 41, subpart D procedures. Petitioner eligibility: any member of the public (including representatives filing on behalf of unnamed principals). Distinguish ex parte (petitioner not entitled to inspect pending application) vs inter partes (petitioner may be privy to contents in reissue-inter partes situations). Petitions by parties to an interference involving the application are generally disallowed post-February 11, 1985, except narrow historical exceptions; public use issues in interferences should be raised by motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(1).
